decisions.title: Liveness is derived once in interpret and feeds both scoring and display
decisions.context: Run-state was display-only (mark.Classify, 2-state ▸/†) and computed after interpret. A dead persistence remnant (disabled .bak + missing target, the com.ironclad.agent case) therefore scored the same as a live, loaded agent, and the mark layer re-derived a run-state the scorer never saw — a DRY split that could drift.
decisions.decision: interpret.livenessState derives a 3-state run-state (active ▸ / armed ◐ / dormant †) once, against the live-process set passed into Assess, and stores it on Assessment.Liveness. recommend() caps a dormant subject at Monitor (it cannot execute) unless a tripwire fires; active/armed keep the score-based recommendation (down-weight the dead, never up-weight the live). mark.Classify now only maps that single value to a glyph and adds the socket mark. This reverses the earlier 'liveness never influences scoring' invariant, but only ever to LOWER urgency, so it cannot manufacture a false escalation. Assess itself stays I/O-free — the caller collects running paths — so verdicts remain reproducible from (findings, running).
consequences: A dead remnant no longer reads as urgently as a live agent
Scored and displayed run-state are the same value — cannot disagree
armed ◐ distinguishes loaded-not-running from dormant in the UI
A --from snapshot carries its scan-time liveness, not a re-derivation against a different machine
Liveness can only reduce a recommendation, never escalate — no new false-positive surface

decisions.title: The scoring engine is a pure function
decisions.context: Scoring is the risk center; it must be testable and free of side effects so weights can be tuned with confidence.
decisions.decision: internal/score is a pure Score([]Evidence) []Finding with no I/O — collectors do all I/O at the edge, so the entire brain is unit-tested from fixtures.
consequences: Weights live only in weights.go (no magic numbers)

decisions.title: Quarantine moves, never deletes
decisions.context: A false positive on an irreversible delete could destroy data or brick the Mac.
decisions.decision: Quarantine only disables and MOVES artifacts into a timestamped mirror with a manifest; restore round-trips byte-identically and refuses to clobber. Permanent deletion is a separate human step outside the tool.
consequences: Manifest is the undo and the RCA trail

decisions.title: Verdicts are rule-based, not model-generated
decisions.context: The tool recommends quarantining people's software; its recommendations must be reproducible and auditable.
decisions.decision: internal/interpret derives verdict/category/recommendation from deterministic rules over the evidence — no LLM in the decision path — so a reviewer (or the ABORT gate) can confirm or refute every label.
consequences: Synthesis lives in the core so CLI/TUI share it

decisions.title: Process evidence is keyed by PID, not argv[0]
decisions.context: argv[0] is attacker-controlled; using it as identity let a malicious listener alias onto an allowlisted app and be suppressed.
decisions.decision: Process evidence uses a PID-only Subject; argv[0] is kept only as a display fact. Safe real-path resolution is deferred (ticket T-4).
consequences: A listener cannot hide by spoofing a trusted path
Process/binary correlation is weaker until T-4

decisions.title: Inspection tells the truth about coverage and shows the wire bytes
decisions.context: An inspector that overstates ('encrypted') or hides ('nothing to view') undermines the tool's credibility. A cleartext binary payload once read as 'ENCRYPTED (TLS)' because its bytes looked like ciphertext.
decisions.decision: 'Encrypted (TLS)' requires positive evidence (a ClientHello SNI, a TLS record, or a well-known TLS port), never merely non-printable bytes. Captured bytes are always shown — readable text as text, cleartext-binary as a hexdump — while TLS ciphertext is withheld as noise. This revises the earlier §6 'never render encrypted' rule, which over-hid.
consequences: Verdicts match reality (no false TLS labels)
The actual outbound payload is inspectable, even when binary
Secrets in readable text still masked until reveal
